items.text: Here is where the two exam families actually overlap, and where they genuinely split.
Most "SSC vs bank exams" content treats this as a pure difficulty ranking.

blocks.heading: Framework If You Can Only Pick One

items.text: If you have genuinely limited time and can only prepare seriously for one track this cycle, run through this order:
If rural or semi-urban branch posting is a genuine non-starter for your family situation, that alone can settle the decision toward SSC.
If you need more attempt opportunities per year to feel secure about the risk, bank exams (IBPS plus SBI plus RRB) give you more cycles.

blocks.heading: Mistakes to Avoid When Making This Decision

items.text: Quant, reasoning, and English overlap enough that light cross-preparation is fine, but static GK, banking awareness, and each exam's specific pattern and difficulty curve are different enough that splitting serious mock-test time across both usually means being mediocre at both instead of strong at one.
A screenshot of an SBI PO CTC figure or an SSC CGL Assistant Commissioner's eventual pay level is not the entry-level reality.
Bank branch postings and SSC departmental transfers are structural, not optional extras.

blocks.heading: What SSC and Bank Exams Actually Cover
rows: What it actually is

A recruitment channel for central government departments, Income Tax, Central Excise/GST, Customs, CBI, Ministry of External Affairs, Audit and Accounts, and dozens of others, through SSC CGL (graduate-level, Group B/C posts) and SSC CHSL (12th-pass-level, Group C posts like LDC/JSA and DEO).

A recruitment channel for public sector bank officer and clerk posts through IBPS (common exam for 11 public sector banks) and SBI's own separate PO and Clerk exams. You end up working inside one specific bank, not a general government cadre.
Number of exams to track
One conducting body (SSC) with two main exams (CGL and CHSL) plus a few specialised ones (CPO, JE, Stenographer). One notification cycle a year for CGL.

Two separate systems: IBPS PO/Clerk (covers 11 banks in one exam) and SBI PO/Clerk (SBI runs its own separate exam). Many aspirants sit both, plus RRB and regional rural bank exams, in the same prep cycle.
Posting variety

Postings spread across dozens of departments and cities depending on the post you get; some roles (Customs, IB) mean port cities or metros, others (Inspector of Income Tax) mean district or state postings.
Postings are branch-based within one bank's network, which can include rural and semi-urban branches, especially in your first few years, this is a structural part of the role, not an exception.

blocks.heading: Syllabus Overlap Between SSC and Bank Exams
rows: Quantitative Aptitude / Numerical Ability

Heavy overlap in basics, percentages, ratios, profit and loss, time and work, simple/compound interest, averages. SSC CGL Tier 1 adds more geometry, trigonometry, and mensuration than bank prelims typically test.
Reasoning

Very high overlap, both test coding-decoding, series, syllogisms, seating arrangement, and puzzles. Bank exams (especially Mains) push puzzle and seating-arrangement difficulty noticeably higher than SSC.
English Language
High overlap in grammar, vocabulary, cloze test, and reading comprehension formats. Difficulty level is broadly comparable across both at the prelims/Tier 1 stage.
General Awareness / GK
Low overlap. SSC leans on static GK, history, polity, geography, science, while bank exams (Mains) focus on banking and financial awareness, current economic affairs, and RBI/monetary policy topics.
Computer Knowledge
Bank Mains includes a dedicated computer knowledge section; SSC CGL does not test this as a separate section for most posts.
Descriptive/Tier 3 writing

SSC CGL has a Tier 2 descriptive paper (essay/letter) for most posts. Bank PO Mains has a descriptive test (essay/letter) too, both require English writing practice, but the topics and word limits differ.

blocks.heading: Difficulty and Competition, Honestly
rows: Recent vacancy volume

SSC CGL 2026 was notified for roughly 12,256 vacancies across departments. IBPS PO 2026 was notified for roughly 6,715 vacancies across 11 public sector banks, and SBI PO 2026 separately for roughly 1,500 vacancies. SSC currently offers the larger single vacancy pool of the three.
Applicant pool size

SSC CGL routinely draws well over 25-40 lakh applicants nationwide because it is open to a very wide range of graduates chasing a wide range of departments. Bank PO exams (IBPS combined) typically draw a somewhat smaller applicant pool, commonly cited in the 15-25 lakh range, spread across fewer, more narrowly defined roles.
Selection ratio

Both land in a similar rough zone, commonly cited estimates put SSC CGL selection odds near 1 in 250-300 applicants and IBPS PO odds near 1 in 300-350, though the exact ratio shifts every cycle with vacancy count and applicant volume. Neither exam is an easy tier to clear; both reward sustained, structured preparation over shortcuts.

blocks.heading: Pay and Career Growth Compared
rows: SSC CGL (central govt, Group B/C)

Entry-level posts sit around Pay Level 4 (Rs 25,500-81,100 basic band) up to Pay Level 7 (Rs 44,900-1,42,400 basic band) depending on the post. In-hand gross pay typically runs roughly Rs 35,000-65,000 a month depending on post, city, and HRA.
SSC CHSL (central govt, Group C)
Lower entry band than CGL, LDC/JSA and DEO posts start meaningfully below CGL's Pay Level 4-7 range, since CHSL is pitched at the 12th-pass level rather than graduate level.
IBPS PO (public sector bank officer)
Basic pay starts around Rs 48,480 and can rise to roughly Rs 85,920 with scheduled increments. Initial in-hand pay, including allowances, is commonly reported in the Rs 74,000-76,000 a month range.
SBI PO (State Bank of India officer)

Initial in-hand pay is commonly reported around Rs 80,000-82,000 a month, with a total CTC figure often quoted near Rs 21-22 lakh a year in metro postings once every allowance and benefit is included.

blocks.heading: SSC CGL Vs IBPS Clerk
rows: Who can apply
CGL needs a graduate degree; CHSL needs Class 12.
A graduate degree in any stream.
Where you work
Central government departments and offices, with the posting depending on the post and the department.
A bank branch in the state you applied for, usually with a local-language test.
Exam stages
Tiered computer-based tests, with skill or typing tests for some CHSL posts.
Preliminary and main computer-based tests, then a language test in the local language.
Pay and growth
A government pay level with a clear promotion ladder and fixed pay bands.
A bank pay scale with a clerk-to-officer ladder through internal exams.
Everyday work
Office, accounts or data-entry work in a department.
Customer-facing counter, cash and account work at a branch.
How we rate it
Not so scalable. A fixed ladder, with growth capped by posts and pay bands.
Not so scalable. A fixed ladder, with a customer-facing skill set that can support a side business or advisory skill.
